title: Energy-Flow Cosmology: A Thermodynamic Bridge Between General Relativity and Quantum Field Theory
description: Introduces Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), a thermodynamic framework in which a continuous energy-flow potential Ef and a normalized entropy field S ∈ [0,1] jointly govern physics. GR and QFT emerge as limiting behaviors as S → 0 and S → 1, respectively, with an entropy-dependent effective light speed c(S) linking macroscopic curvature and microscopic quantization. The paper outlines observable implications for cosmology, including lensing without dark matter, Hubble-tension reinterpretation, and measurable deviations in c under extreme field conditions.

variable_speed_of_light.description: Phenomenological relation positing that the effective speed of coherent information/light depends on local entropy density S, with c(S) approaching the conventional vacuum value c0 as S → 0 and decreasing as disorder grows.

entropy_domain.description: Normalized entropy field specifying local degree of equilibrium; S≈0 corresponds to ordered/coherent domains, S≈1 to disordered/probabilistic domains.

regime_limits.latex: S \to 0:\; \text{GR-like continuous geometry}\quad;\quad S \to 1:\; \text{QFT-like probabilistic quantization}
regime_limits.description: Mapping of entropy limits to emergent physical regimes: low-entropy domains reproduce GR behavior, high-entropy domains reproduce QFT behavior.

energy_flow_potential.latex: E_f,\quad \nabla E_f \;\text{encodes local exchange of momentum and curvature}
energy_flow_potential.description: Defines a continuous scalar–vector energy-flow potential whose gradient mediates directional energy transfer and curvature coupling across scales.

key_results.main_finding: Proposes a unified, non-equilibrium thermodynamic field theory in which an entropy-dependent light speed c(S) and an energy-flow potential Ef make GR and QFT emergent boundary regimes and recast dark sector anomalies as entropic stresses.

sealed_predictions.statement: Effective propagation speed of coherent signals exhibits environment/entropy dependence c(S), leading to measurable deviations in time-of-flight or dispersion across high-entropy vs low-entropy sightlines under extreme field conditions.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-wavelength, multi-messenger timing and Shapiro-delay measurements through clusters/ICM vs voids showing no deviations from GR plus known plasma effects when stratified by entropy proxies.

sealed_predictions.statement: Strong lensing and galaxy dynamics in systems with mapped entropy gradients can be fit without invoking collisionless dark matter when entropic stresses from EFC are included.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Comprehensive lensing and rotation-curve reconstructions across clusters and galaxies that remain inconsistent with any plausible entropic-stress model tied to observed thermodynamic structure.

sealed_predictions.statement: The inferred Hubble constant exhibits an environmental/entropy correlation arising from c(S) and entropic redshift contributions, offering a thermodynamic explanation of the Hubble tension.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Standard-candle/siren H0 measurements stratified by large-scale structure (voids vs clusters) showing no statistically significant correlation with entropy proxies beyond selection/systematics.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB anisotropy patterns can reflect imprints of large-scale entropy gradients consistent with EFC without requiring a separate dark energy component.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: CMB power spectra and lensing reconstructions that cannot be jointly fit by any EFC-consistent entropy-gradient parameterization while matching BAO and SN distance ladders.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision time-of-flight and Shapiro-delay measurements across paths that traverse demonstrably different entropy environments (e.g., hot ICM vs cosmic voids), after correcting for GR and plasma dispersion, show no environment-dependent deviations in photon propagation compatible with any reasonable c(S) coupling.

KC2: Galaxy–galaxy and cluster strong-lensing mass maps and rotation curves, when jointly modeled with observed thermodynamic profiles (e.g., X-ray/SZ-derived entropy maps), still require collisionless dark matter in a way irreconcilable with any entropic-stress contribution from EFC across a large, controlled sample.
KC3: CMB, BAO, and SN datasets jointly rule out all EFC-consistent c(S) and entropy-gradient parameterizations that could reproduce ΛCDM-level fits, leaving no viable region of EFC parameter space.

KC4: Targeted tests of quantum-to-classical crossover in ultra-low-entropy, macroscopically coherent systems reveal no trend toward increased continuity/GR-like behavior consistent with the S → 0 limit, contrary to EFC’s entropy-regime mapping, after controlling for decoherence and environmental noise.
